The device's death did not free it. LUMA (radio, sharp): 'Theodore — don't move. The device is dead but the network isn't. There's an eighth contact. It's not crystalline. It's organic. Panel 4 — CRIBBAGE, removal-mechanics setup, MECHANICAL NOT MEDICAL (NEW) — Theodore's hands move to the nape; Wren's copper-gold guide swings from the cabinet to a new target overlay on the plug; Luma's blue-violet vitals readout floats beside it. LUMA: 'This is everything. Every glyph. Every trace. Every story. I've mapped them.'

Panel 2 — Luma traces the operatives-and-stories threads, two connections fused (KEPT/CONDENSED from current P17 P2+P3) — one panel now carries both traces: glyph→cache→operatives (they chose to stay) AND cache→newspapers→pamphlet (the stories are the record). LUMA: 'Prior operatives — at least three deployments over centuries. Each one carved glyphs. Each one stayed. And everywhere they went, stories followed. Humans saw them, told stories, published them. The fairy tales aren't incidental. They're the record. They're what persists.'

Panel 3 — Wren's pushback / Jink's realization, the two reactions fused (KEPT/CONDENSED from current P17 P4+P5) — split-focus panel: Wren arms-crossed skeptical on one side, Jink seeing the purpose on the other. WREN: 'Stories don't build civilizations, Luma. Technology does.' / LUMA: 'The telegraph carries information that shapes what people believe. The medium shapes the message. The message shapes the civilization.' / JINK: 'So we're not stuck here. We're needed here.'

Panel 4 — Luma delivers the core thesis (KEPT from current P18 P1, the synthesis itself — uncut) — Luma at the center beside the glowing written-page node, the holographic STAY in fairy script beside her, scanner trembling. LUMA: 'The convergence point isn't technological. It's narrative. What humanity believes about the unknown — about fairies, about monsters, about wonder and fear — shapes the civilization they become. Those beliefs are set here, now, in these stories. Our stories. The mission isn't to change an event. The mission is to be here. To be the fairies in the fairy tales. That's the intervention. That's what STAY means.'

outlineEdit.oldText: **Theodore's moment.** He can reach the last device. It's inside a telegraph relay station, human-scaled, human-accessible. Wren talks him through the disarm over a holographic comm link. His clever hands — oil-stained, burn-scarred, trained on clockwork — do the work. He is ordinary in an extraordinary moment.
outlineEdit.newText: **Theodore's moment.** He can reach the last device — a human-scaled Titan node in a street telegraph exchange. Wren talks him through the disarm over a holographic comm link; his clever hands, trained on clockwork, do the work. But killing the device doesn't end it: Luma, monitoring the network, reads an eighth contact — not crystalline but organic, a brain-plug in a slumped man wired to the same node. Theodore turns and it is CRIBBAGE, his master — one of the five plugged humans (discovered Issues 9–10; this is recognition, not discovery). In a single unbroken motion — Wren guiding the geometry, Luma calling vitals, mechanical not medical, lethal if torqued — Theodore eases the plug from the nape by hand. Cribbage surfaces with the first simple, lost words ('my hands'): recovery, not death — the only one of the five freed in Volume 1. The power inverts; the master who dismissed him now needs him, and Theodore chooses to stay and get him *home* — paying the Issue 11 'chosen back' by choosing back, unwitnessed by the indifferent street. He is ordinary in an extraordinary moment. *(Stage only the freeing, the first signs, and the choice here; the weeks-after domestic recovery — 'no one knows who freed him' — is Volume 2, Issue 1, where Cribbage and Theodore reconcile.)*
